rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes in-situ preheating and dynamic laser power modulation during LPBF, whereas the paper uses atmosphere-controlled debinding and solid-state sintering of DLP-printed green bodies. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies LPBF under ambient conditions with preheating and laser modulation, while the paper uses DLP printing, debinding in oxygen-rich vs. oxygen-deficient atmospheres, and furnace sintering at 800–1100 °C. The processing regimes are entirely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes reduced thermal gradients and refined microstructure via melt-pool control, whereas the paper's mechanism involves carbon retention, reduced gas evolution, and oxide-layer effects on diffusion and densification during solid-state sintering. These are different classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved dimensional precision and mechanical properties (yield strength, crack resistance) relative to standard LPBF, while the paper reports earlier densification and comparable compressive strength at a lower sintering temperature with reduced surface cracking. The predicted properties and comparisons differ.
